text: {"overall_winner": "B", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Direct quotations from the article woven into each body paragraph with clear attribution", "quality": "Use of textual evidence", "description": "Essay B integrates specific quoted details from the source article to support each point, whereas Essay A only loosely paraphrases or references article content."}, {"evidence": "Clear structure with an introduction posing a question, three body paragraphs each with a distinct point, and a conclusion", "quality": "Organizational coherence", "description": "Essay B follows a consistent paragraph structure where each body paragraph develops one focused argument, while Essay A's ideas are scattered and repetitive across paragraphs."}, {"evidence": "Each body paragraph opens with a topic sentence and then explains how the evidence supports the anti-driverless position", "quality": "Argumentative reasoning", "description": "Essay B consistently connects evidence back to its thesis by explaining why each detail demonstrates danger or unreliability, whereas Essay A largely summarizes article facts without building a sustained case."}, {"evidence": "Correct spelling and standard sentence construction throughout", "quality": "Conventions and clarity", "description": "Essay B is written in largely standard English with proper spelling and punctuation, while Essay A contains numerous spelling errors and run-on sentences that impede readability."}, {"evidence": "A consistent stance against driverless cars maintained from introduction through conclusion", "quality": "Focused thesis development", "description": "Essay B states its position clearly at the start and reinforces it in every paragraph, whereas Essay A shifts between enthusiasm and hedging, weakening its overall argument."}]}
